architecture.text: Practitioners are deploying advanced techniques like HySparse2 and GTR alongside hyperbolic quantization and block-level MoE conditioning to overcome long-context agent bottlenecks, memory limits, and attention inefficiencies.

new-models.text: Recent work highlights Xiaomi MiMo-V2.6-Pro 1T-A42B alongside flow-based generative models, foundation model embeddings, mixture-of-experts, and vision-language agents advancing multimodal and cross-scenario physical intelligence.

inference-methods.text: Practitioners are scaling test-time compute, sub-3-bit on-policy distillation, disaggregated quantization, and CompKV and GeoPair compression to run massive contexts on consumer hardware like 24 GiB laptops.

inference-engines.text: Recent inference optimization focuses on NVIDIA Topograph, Flux, and SARA, targeting memory tiering, topology-aware scheduling, and SLO-driven resource allocation for complex agentic workloads.

silicon.text: Engineers are maximizing TPU, GPU, and FPGA efficiency, pushing HBM profiling, DRAM and SSD offloading, wafer-scale superconducting transistors, and optical interconnects to scale massive AI clusters.

training.text: Practitioners are tackling reward hacking and credit assignment across reinforcement learning, scaling laws, and diffusion models using techniques like group relative policy optimization and rubric rewards.

economics.text: Inference costs are collapsing industry-wide through 40 to 50 percent price cuts and plunging token economics, driving the shift toward self-hosted open-weight models.
